name: Hannah
description: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy

points: There was a certain man of mount Ephraim named Elkanah, and he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: When Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions; but unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion, for he loved Hannah: but the Lord had shut up her womb.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Hannah could not conceive while her husband's other wife could, and he asked her, Am not I better to thee than ten sons?

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

points: Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and in bitterness of soul she prayed unto the Lord and wept sore, while Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: As she continued praying before the Lord, Eli marked her mouth. Hannah spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken, and said, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Hannah answered, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord; count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial. Then Eli answered, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: They rose up in the morning early, worshipped before the Lord, and returned to their house to Ramah; they went back up north, for Elkanah came out of mount Ephraim. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife: knew means he laid with her, they had laid down together; and the Lord remembered her.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: When the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, she bare a son and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord. Samuel means asked of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: But Hannah went not up; she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the Lord, and there abide for ever. A weaned child was three or four years old; that would be the last time he was under her care, so she said, I am not going up until that happens.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

points: Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

cases.name: Hannah
cases.charge: Pouring out her soul before the Lord, vowing a son to him, and lending him to the Lord as long as he liveth
cases.preview: Elkanah had two wives; Peninnah had children, and Hannah had none, for the Lord had closed her womb, and her rival taunted her year after year at the house of the Lord until she wept and would not eat.
